findings.reason: The protected solution is clear, conventional, and interview-ready for the source domain. Its explicit three-phase postorder frame avoids recursion-depth failure, returns exactly the increasing and decreasing arms required by the recurrence, and combines them at each node without storing per-node maps or rebuilding paths.

A child contributes only when its value is exactly one above or below its parent. The longest matching arm of each direction is retained across both children, and increasing + decreasing - 1 joins opposite arms through their shared highest node. Every valid path has one such highest node, while every combined pair is an actual simple monotone consecutive path.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 549 and its Python longestConsecutive(root) interface. The app-local TreeNode is the required explicit local equivalent of LeetCode's injected model, solve(root) returns a node count, and its defensive empty-root result does not alter the legal nonempty source domain.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065350528 have the same phase transitions, child-result slots, directional recurrence, maximum update, parent-result propagation, and return value. Their only structural difference is the app-local TreeNode definition and its explanatory frame comment.

The repaired benchmark uses legal 255-, 2047-, and 16383-node consecutive chains that expose repeated finalized-result scans. The exact protected source passed all 10 refreshed correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including the legal 30,000-node deep-tree boundary. The correct quadratic rescan control passed every benchmark output but failed only scaling with relative growth exponent +0.31.

The Approach exactly matches the protected target: two directional arms, edge-difference checks, an opposite-arm join at each highest node, and explicit postorder phase handling. Its O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary-space claims correctly account for one finalization per node and one active frame per tree level.

The modular Reference was reviewed directly in the authenticated Premium statement and bound to its rendered live-content hash. It preserves the increasing/decreasing rule, the valid and invalid sequence examples, child-parent-child permission, both explained examples, both constraints, and both source tree relationships through accessible Mermaid diagrams.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples appear first and in source order with their exact three-node trees and expected lengths 2 and 3.
The invented singleton sample was relabelled as a trial, and the formerly hidden decreasing-chain, equal-value, and below-root checks are now visible trials.
Contract boundaries cover one and 30,000 nodes, values -30000 and 30000, shallow balanced trees, one-sided deep trees, and the full legal node-count maximum without relying on recursion.

Material semantics cover increasing and decreasing direction, child-parent-child turns, a longest path strictly below the root, exact difference one, equal-value nonextension, one-arm answers, two-arm joins, and direction consistency.

An independent graph oracle oriented each tree edge from value x to x + 1 and found the longest path in the resulting DAG for all ten correctness cases and all three benchmarks. The protected app and immutable native sources also agreed on 107,724 exhaustive shape/value trees and 1,000 randomized trees.
All ten correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 255-, 2047-, and 16383-node consecutive-chain workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
